lines.text: **Security:** v1 trusts the LAN. There are no credentials: a link exchanges addresses and authorizes nothing, and IP checks can be spoofed. That is why the built-in plugins only read information. Plugins that act on the computer (keys, launching apps) wait for the credential decision in [ADR 0004](../../../docs/adr/0004-host-control-sliced-delivery.md).

lines.text: Serves `POST /command` on every interface, port 8797. The port never moves to a free one, because the Vita stores the URL; if it is busy, `start` exits with an error. It prints its URLs, the loaded plugins, and one line per request (time, peer, `plugin.command`, result, duration). Payloads are never logged.

lines.summary: feat(shell): one LAN Listener for upload and link, on from startup
lines.text: Pass the Vita's address: VitaDeck listens from startup, and the VitaDeck Shell shows the address under Upload and link (add `:port` if it is not 8787). `link` checks that `start` is answering, then tells VitaDeck where to send commands. One Vita can link several computers, and one computer can link several Vitas.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: feat(host-companion): Host Companion CLI and system-stats plugin

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: feat(host-control): the companion relinks its Vitas on every start
lines.text: Each `start` relinks every Vita this computer linked, so a new IP or `--port` reaches them without running `link` again. A Vita that is off is retried every 30 s; one that forgot this computer in the Shell is dropped from the config instead of being linked again. A Vita whose Upload and link listener moved off port 8787 needs `link` again.

lines.text: Sends a notice to every Deck App watching this computer's `core` events (the `host-control` demo shows it), for example at the end of a script: `make && vitadeck-host-companion notify "Build done"`. Deck Apps keep one request waiting at the companion for events, renewed every 25 s while nothing happens, so the request log shows a `core.events` line about every 25 s per watching Deck App.

lines.text: `install` unpacks the archive (or copies a `.vdplugin` folder) into `~/.vitadeck/plugins/`, named by the plugin's id, and a running companion loads it at once. A plugin runs with your permissions on this computer, so install only plugins you trust.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.summary: feat(sdk): Host Plugins can be authored without a Deck App
lines.text: To write one, scaffold a Deck App with `npx @vitadeck/sdk create my-app --host-plugin`, or a plugin on its own with `create my-plugin --host-plugin-only`; the [SDK README](../sdk/README.md#your-own-host-plugin) explains the files. While you work on it, `start --plugin ./dist` loads your build, takes precedence over an installed copy, and reloads every time `vitadeck build` or `vitadeck dev` writes it. A broken build keeps the previous version running.

lines.text: The Vita connects to the companion, so the computer must accept incoming connections on the port. The first `start` triggers a prompt: on macOS, allow `node` to accept incoming network connections; on Windows, allow Node.js on private networks. On Linux, open the port in your firewall if one is running (`sudo ufw allow 8797/tcp`).
